```{r setup}
#| code-summary: "Setup: sample, reliabilities and models"
source(here::here("common.R"))
library(lavaan)

scores_all <- load_levante_latest("scores")
trials <- load_levante_latest("trials")
scores <- clean_levante_latest(scores_all, trials)
data_ref <- unique(scores_all$redivis_source)

core <- c("matrix", "mrot", "math", "hf", "mg", "sds", "trog", "vocab", "tom")
reading <- c("swr", "sre", "pa")
short_labels <- deframe(task_lookup |> select(short, task_label))

# each child's first run of each task
first <- scores |>
  filter(short %in% c(core, reading)) |>
  group_by(dataset, user_id, short) |>
  slice_min(time_started, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

# datasets with 200 or more children who did at least 6 of the 9 core tasks
sample_ds <- first |>
  filter(short %in% core) |>
  group_by(dataset, user_id) |>
  summarise(k = n_distinct(short), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  summarise(full = sum(k >= 6), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(full >= 200) |>
  pull(dataset)

# scores standardized within dataset, so dataset mean differences drop out
first <- first |>
  filter(dataset %in% sample_ds) |>
  group_by(dataset, short) |>
  mutate(z = as.numeric(scale(score))) |>
  ungroup()

# empirical reliability of EAP scores, var / (var + mean SE^2), within
# dataset and averaged weighted by n
reliability <- first |>
  filter(!is.na(score_se)) |>
  group_by(dataset, short) |>
  summarise(rel = var(score) / (var(score) + mean(score_se^2)), n = n(),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(short) |>
  summarise(rel = weighted.mean(rel, n)) |>
  deframe()

age_first <- first |>
  filter(!is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(user_id) |>
  summarise(age = min(age))
wide <- first |>
  select(dataset, user_id, short, z) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = short, values_from = z) |>
  left_join(age_first, by = "user_id") |>
  mutate(age_c = age - mean(age, na.rm = TRUE))
wide_age <- filter(wide, !is.na(age))

fit_index <- \(f, m) as.numeric(fitMeasures(f, m))
improper <- function(f) {
  pe <- parameterEstimates(f)
  any(pe$est[pe$op == "~~" & pe$lhs == pe$rhs] < -1e-4) ||
    any(abs(subset(standardizedSolution(f), op == "=~")$est.std) > 1.001)
}
fv_cor <- function(f) {
  parameterEstimates(f) |> filter(lhs == "fluid", op == "~~", rhs == "verbal")
}

models <- list(
  `g` = "g =~ matrix+mrot+math+hf+mg+sds+trog+vocab+tom",
  `2-factor` = "fluid =~ matrix+mrot+math+hf+mg+sds\n verbal =~ trog+vocab+tom",
  `3-factor` = "reasoning =~ matrix+mrot+math\n ef =~ hf+mg+sds\n language =~ trog+vocab+tom",
  `bifactor` = "g =~ matrix+mrot+math+hf+mg+sds+trog+vocab+tom
                reasoning =~ matrix+mrot+math\n ef =~ hf+mg+sds\n language =~ trog+vocab+tom")
fits <- imap(models, \(m, nm) cfa(m, wide, std.lv = TRUE, missing = "fiml",
                                  orthogonal = nm == "bifactor"))
comparison <- imap_dfr(fits, \(f, nm) tibble(
  model = nm, CFI = fit_index(f, "cfi"), RMSEA = fit_index(f, "rmsea"),
  BIC = fit_index(f, "bic"), proper = !improper(f)))
best <- comparison |> filter(proper) |> slice_min(BIC, n = 1)
fit2 <- fits[["2-factor"]]
fit3 <- fits[["3-factor"]]

# corrected task correlations: each task a latent with error variance fixed
# from its reliability
silv <- paste(c(sprintf("eta_%s =~ 1*%s", core, core),
                sprintf("%s ~~ %.4f*%s", core, pmax(1 - reliability[core], .02), core)),
              collapse = "\n")
cor_corrected <- lavInspect(cfa(silv, wide, missing = "fiml"), "cor.lv")
dimnames(cor_corrected) <- list(short_labels[core], short_labels[core])

# the one-, two- and three-factor models in each dataset
per_dataset <- map_dfr(sample_ds, \(ds) imap_dfr(models[1:3], function(m, nm) {
  f <- cfa(m, filter(wide, dataset == ds), std.lv = TRUE, missing = "fiml")
  tibble(model = nm, BIC = fit_index(f, "bic"), proper = !improper(f))
}) |> mutate(dataset = ds, dBIC = BIC - min(BIC)))

two_best <- per_dataset |> filter(model == "2-factor")

# invariance of the two-factor model across datasets and age bands
ladder <- function(data, group) {
  levels <- list(configural = NULL, metric = "loadings",
                 scalar = c("loadings", "intercepts"))
  imap_dfr(levels, \(eq, nm) {
    f <- cfa(models[["2-factor"]], data, group = group, group.equal = eq,
             std.lv = TRUE, missing = "fiml")
    tibble(level = nm, CFI = fit_index(f, "cfi"), RMSEA = fit_index(f, "rmsea"))
  }) |> mutate(dCFI = CFI - lag(CFI))
}
ladder_ds <- ladder(wide, "dataset") |> slice(1:2)
age_bins <- c(0, 7, 9, 11, 20)
wide_bins <- wide_age |>
  mutate(age_bin = cut(age, age_bins, labels = c("under 7", "7–9", "9–11", "11 and over")))
ladder_age <- ladder(wide_bins, "age_bin")

# fluid-verbal correlation below and above each dataset's median age
young_old <- wide_age |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  group_modify(function(d, key) {
    split <- median(d$age)
    y <- fv_cor(cfa(models[["2-factor"]], filter(d, age < split), std.lv = TRUE, missing = "fiml"))
    o <- fv_cor(cfa(models[["2-factor"]], filter(d, age >= split), std.lv = TRUE, missing = "fiml"))
    tibble(split = split, younger = y$est, younger_se = y$se,
           older = o$est, older_se = o$se)
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(diff = younger - older, diff_se = sqrt(younger_se^2 + older_se^2),
         lo = diff - 1.96 * diff_se, hi = diff + 1.96 * diff_se)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Summary

**Data:** `r data_ref`; each child's first run of each task in the
`r length(sample_ds)` datasets with 200 or more children who did at least 6
of the 9 core tasks (`r fmt_n(nrow(wide))` children). Scores are
standardized within dataset.

- The nine core tasks share a strong general factor. Corrected for
  measurement error, every pair of tasks correlates between
  `r f2(min(cor_corrected[upper.tri(cor_corrected)]))` and
  `r f2(max(cor_corrected[upper.tri(cor_corrected)]))`.
- Beyond it, the data support two correlated abilities: a fluid ability
  (reasoning, spatial, math and executive tasks) and a verbal one (sentence
  understanding, vocabulary and Stories), correlating
  r = `r f2(fv_cor(fit2)$est)`. The two-factor model has the lowest BIC among
  proper models, and splitting reasoning from executive function adds
  nothing (those two factors correlate
  r = `r f2(lavInspect(fit3, "cor.lv")["reasoning", "ef"])`).
- The two-factor model has the lowest BIC in
  `r sum(two_best$dBIC == 0)` of the `r length(sample_ds)` datasets and is
  at most `r round(max(two_best$dBIC))` BIC points behind in the others. Its
  loadings can be held equal across datasets
  (ΔCFI = `r sprintf("%.3f", ladder_ds$dCFI[2])`) and across ages
  (ΔCFI = `r sprintf("%.3f", ladder_age$dCFI[2])`).
- Younger children's fluid and verbal abilities are more strongly correlated
  than older children's in `r sum(young_old$diff > 0)` of
  `r nrow(young_old)` datasets, reliably so only in
  `r paste(dataset_labels_named[young_old$dataset[young_old$lo > 0]], collapse = ", ")`.
:::

# Task correlations, corrected for measurement error

Most constructs here have a single task, so a task's reliable specific
variance is mixed with its error. To separate them, each task becomes a
latent variable whose error variance is fixed from its empirical
reliability, and the latent correlations are read off.

```{r corrected-correlations, fig.height=5.5}
as.data.frame(cor_corrected) |>
  rownames_to_column("t1") |>
  pivot_longer(-t1, names_to = "t2", values_to = "r") |>
  mutate(t1 = factor(t1, rev(short_labels[core])), t2 = factor(t2, short_labels[core]),
         r = if_else(t1 == t2, NA_real_, r)) |>
  ggplot(aes(t2, t1, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(r), "", f2(r)), colour = r > .6), size = 3.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(na.value = "grey92", name = "r") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))
```

The reliabilities used range from `r f2(min(reliability[core]))`
(`r short_labels[names(which.min(reliability[core]))]`) to
`r f2(max(reliability[core]))`
(`r short_labels[names(which.max(reliability[core]))]`). The highest
corrected correlation is between Sentence Understanding and Vocabulary
(r = `r f2(cor_corrected["Sentence Understanding", "Vocabulary"])`); Stories
correlates `r f2(cor_corrected["Stories (ToM)", "Sentence Understanding"])`
with Sentence Understanding and
`r f2(cor_corrected["Stories (ToM)", "Vocabulary"])` with Vocabulary, so it
keeps some reliable variance of its own.
`r names(which.min(rowMeans(cor_corrected - diag(NA, nrow(cor_corrected)), na.rm = TRUE)))`
is the most distinct task, with the lowest average correlation with the
others.

# Which structure

Four confirmatory models: one general factor; two factors (fluid: Pattern
Matching, Shape Rotation, Math, Hearts and Flowers, Memory, Same and
Different; verbal: Sentence Understanding, Vocabulary, Stories); three
factors (reasoning, executive function, language); and a bifactor model
(a general factor plus the three domains). With a strong positive manifold,
fit indices keep improving as factors are added, so the models are judged
first on whether the solution is proper, then on BIC.

```{r comparison}
comparison |>
  mutate(across(c(CFI, RMSEA), \(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)), BIC = fmt_n(round(BIC)),
         proper = if_else(proper, "yes", "no")) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Model", "CFI", "RMSEA", "BIC", "Proper"), align = "lrrrc")
```

The `r best$model` model has the lowest BIC. Its standardized loadings:

```{r loadings, fig.height=4.5}
standardizedSolution(fit2) |>
  filter(op == "=~") |>
  mutate(task = factor(short_labels[rhs], rev(short_labels[core])),
         factor = str_to_title(lhs)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = est.std, y = task, colour = factor)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = ci.lower, xmax = ci.upper)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Standardized loading (95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## With the reading tasks

ROAR-Word, ROAR-Sentence and ROAR-Phoneme are not core tasks, but adding
them asks whether reading forms its own ability.

```{r reading}
reading_models <- list(
  `g` = "g =~ matrix+mrot+math+hf+mg+sds+trog+vocab+tom+swr+sre+pa",
  `2-factor, reading in verbal` = "fluid =~ matrix+mrot+math+hf+mg+sds\n verbal =~ trog+vocab+tom+swr+sre+pa",
  `3-factor, separate reading` = "fluid =~ matrix+mrot+math+hf+mg+sds\n verbal =~ trog+vocab+tom\n reading =~ swr+sre+pa")
reading_fits <- map(reading_models, \(m) cfa(m, wide, std.lv = TRUE, missing = "fiml"))
reading_cor <- lavInspect(reading_fits[[3]], "cor.lv")
imap_dfr(reading_fits, \(f, nm) tibble(model = nm, CFI = sprintf("%.3f", fit_index(f, "cfi")),
                                       BIC = fmt_n(round(fit_index(f, "bic"))),
                                       proper = if_else(improper(f), "no", "yes"))) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Model", "CFI", "BIC", "Proper"), align = "lrrc")
```

A separate reading factor has the lowest BIC. It correlates
r = `r f2(reading_cor["reading", "fluid"])` with the fluid ability and
r = `r f2(reading_cor["reading", "verbal"])` with the verbal one, so it is not
specifically tied to language.

# Across datasets

The one-, two- and three-factor models, fitted separately in each dataset:

```{r per-dataset, fig.height=4}
per_dataset |>
  mutate(dataset_label = factor(dataset_labels_named[dataset],
                                rev(dataset_labels_named[sample_ds])),
         model = factor(model, names(models)[1:3])) |>
  mutate(solution = if_else(proper, "proper", "improper")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dBIC, y = dataset_label, colour = model, shape = solution)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(proper = 16, improper = 4), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "pseudo_log") +
  labs(x = "BIC above the best model in that dataset (0 = best)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Holding the two-factor model's loadings equal across the
`r length(sample_ds)` datasets changes CFI by `r sprintf("%.3f", ladder_ds$dCFI[2])`
(from `r sprintf("%.3f", ladder_ds$CFI[1])`), within the usual .01
threshold, so the tasks measure the two abilities in the same way in each
dataset. Because scores are standardized within dataset, a test of equal
intercepts across datasets would not be informative.

# Across age

Holding loadings equal across four age bands
(`r paste(levels(wide_bins$age_bin), collapse = ", ")`) changes CFI by
`r sprintf("%.3f", ladder_age$dCFI[2])`; also holding intercepts equal changes it by a
further `r sprintf("%.3f", ladder_age$dCFI[3])`, as expected when scores rise with age. So
a change in how the abilities relate across age is not an artifact of
loadings drifting.

Within each dataset, the fluid–verbal correlation in children below and
above the dataset's median age (95% CIs):

```{r young-old, fig.height=4}
young_old |>
  select(dataset, split, younger, younger_se, older, older_se) |>
  pivot_longer(c(younger, older), names_to = "group", values_to = "r") |>
  mutate(se = if_else(group == "younger", younger_se, older_se),
         group = factor(group, c("younger", "older"), c("Younger half", "Older half")),
         dataset_label = factor(dataset_labels_named[dataset],
                                rev(dataset_labels_named[sample_ds]))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = r, y = dataset_label, colour = group)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = r - 1.96 * se, xmax = r + 1.96 * se),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#4477AA", "#CC6677"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Fluid–verbal correlation", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The difference is largest in
`r dataset_labels_named[young_old$dataset[which.max(young_old$diff)]]`
(`r f2(max(young_old$diff))`, 95% CI `r f2(young_old$lo[which.max(young_old$diff)])`
to `r f2(young_old$hi[which.max(young_old$diff)])`), and runs the other way
in `r paste(dataset_labels_named[young_old$dataset[young_old$diff < 0]], collapse = " and ")`.
The datasets cover different ages, so the median split falls between
`r round(min(young_old$split), 1)` and `r round(max(young_old$split), 1)`
years.

As a continuous function of age within each dataset (local structural
equation model: each child weighted by a normal kernel around the focal
age, bandwidth 1 year; shown where the effective sample is at least 150):

```{r local-sem, fig.height=5.5}
local_fv <- function(d, ages = seq(6, 12, by = 0.5), h = 1) {
  map_dfr(ages, function(a0) {
    w <- dnorm((d$age - a0) / h)
    if (sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2) < 150) return(NULL)
    f <- tryCatch(cfa(models[["2-factor"]], cbind(d, .w = w / mean(w)), std.lv = TRUE,
                      missing = "fiml", sampling.weights = ".w"),
                  error = \(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(f) || !lavInspect(f, "converged")) return(NULL)
    pe <- fv_cor(f)
    tibble(age = a0, r = pe$est, lo = pe$ci.lower, hi = pe$ci.upper)
  })
}
local <- wide_age |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  group_modify(\(d, key) local_fv(d)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(local, aes(x = age, y = r, colour = dataset, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(lo, 0.4), ymax = pmin(hi, 1)), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(vars(dataset_labels_named[dataset])) +
  scale_colour_dataset(guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_dataset(guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 6:12) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Fluid–verbal correlation")
```

# Notes

- **Sample.** Each child contributes their first run of each task. The
  downward-extension, younger-sibling and smaller datasets have too few
  children with most of the core tasks to fit these models.
- **Standardizing within dataset** removes differences in dataset means, so
  these models describe how tasks covary within datasets, not how datasets
  differ.
- **Proper solutions.** A model is improper when a variance is negative or a
  standardized loading exceeds 1.

# Revision history

- **2026-10-30.** Rewritten on the pinned release, merging "03 — Construct
  structure & measurement invariance" and "04 — Construct structure:
  emergent dimensions, differentiation, and the role of g" (both on the
  2026-08 per-site snapshot of four datasets). Argentina and Sheffield are
  added; scores are now standardized within dataset; MEFS is left out (few
  children have it); and the shared-speed check from 04 is not carried over.
  On the new data Stories is less fully absorbed into the verbal ability than
  the earlier pages reported, and the decline of the fluid–verbal
  correlation with age is clear only in rural Colombia, not in every
  dataset. Both old pages are in `archive/`.
